sources.title: Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'
sources.text: Rockstar made a point of creating "authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality." It's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion. One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life. "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar ). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Humphries says this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6 , Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained. Establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world." This is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts . And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does. sources.text: Sex work is depicted in one form or another in most Grand Theft Auto games, and though you canât hire prostitutes this time around , you can definitely still go to a strip club and see a show in Grand Theft Auto 6 . So where are these fine establishments, and what can you actually do there? Letâs break it down. There are three strip clubs in GTA 6 , and you actually wonât have to go looking for them because the main story will bring you to all of them. Thereâs Delights Cabaret, NINE1NINE, and Jack of Hearts. The first one is in Port Gellhorn where youâll spend the majority of the gameâs second chapter, and the other two are in Vice City proper.Â You can visit any of these locations as either Jason or Lucia, and both can participate in their services. You can shake it on the dancefloor and make it rain on the performers if you have cash on-hand. However, if you want something a little more private, you can hire performers for a private dance by holding down the left trigger to interact with them and paying their fee. Jason and Lucia can do this together or separately, though it will cost more for both of them to join in on the fun than it is for a solo show, and doing so doesnât seem to have any negative bearing on their relationshipÂ At the moment, Iâve been able to confirm that Lucia is able to get a lap dance from female dancers, but I havenât seen any evidence that Jason can receive them from men. Thus far, the only male dancers Iâve found in the game were those who perform during the âAfternoon Delightâ mission, which features them prevalently and lets the player get a first-person lap dance from a male dancer. However, it doesnât appear that you can seek them out whenever you want like you can the women. My gut reaction is to assume that this is so players canât make Jason do gay stuff, and thatâs a huge bummer for a game that seems to be pretty open-minded and is obviously willing to let Lucia engage in some same-sex services. Jason and Lucia seem more than willing to enjoy sexy entertainment together, and can have plenty of sex at home if youâre nurturing their relationship.Â Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a 'complex drug network' that tracks everything from where drugs come from to 'how they eventually reach the street-level buyer'
sources.text: "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real." I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood. I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6 's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN , Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom. "A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer." Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there." While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. But it's such commitment to representing its world that has led GTA 6 to receive near-universal praise from critics, and it probably didn't hurt when it earned $3.79 billion on launch day , either. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has received a new update which fixes autosaving
sources.text: The new patch fixes other bugs, including being unable to lose Wanted Levels Grand Theft Auto 6 has received its first post-launch patch, fixing a number of bugs in the game. The update, which is around 603 MB in size and brings the game up to version 01.002.002, fixes a number of issues including problems players have been having with autosaves. Players have been reporting issues with autosaving since the game’s release, with some saying they experienced save data loss resulting in the initial portion of their progress in the game disappearing. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. While the game auto-saves after major single-player missions and some side-missions, it appears that this has been inconsistent, with some players reporting that even though they had been completing the main missions in the early hours of GTA 6, the auto save function wasn’t working as intended. The hope will be that the latest update will resolve some of these issues and ensure auto-saving works more reliably. VGC advises players to pause and manually save the game to be sure. VGCâs Grand Theft Auto 6 review calls it âthe game of the generationâ, saying Rockstar âdelivers its modern masterpiece with a remarkable artistic achievement that exceeds all expectationsâ. âRockstarâs developers have created a remarkable open world that excels in storytelling, gameplay, visuals, music and technology to achieve something truly unmatched,â we wrote. âMinor performance issues donât dull the sparkle of an absolute must-play experience. GTA 6 was more than worth the wait.â

sources.title: Has Rockstar taken the "Grand Theft Auto" out of GTA 6? Or has it just gamified car-jacking properly for the first time?
sources.text: It's impossible to have a big game launch these days without some section of the internet, somewhere, finding grievances with the final product because it does not align with the expectations they had pre-release. The most recent upset comes in the form of Grand Theft Auto 6 's revised take on, well, grand theft auto. In case you're one of the few still unfamiliar, grand theft auto is more than the titular moniker for Rockstar's premier crime simulation series; it's actually a US legal term for the act of stealing or attempting to steal a motor vehicle. In most previous GTA entries, this was a central part of the core gameplay loop: accept a mission, nick a car, complete the mission, nick another car, getaway. It's an endemic part of the loop, and has become so popular and identifiable as such that even other games - Watch Dogs , Saint's Row, Cyberpunk 2077 , and so on - have emulated the mechanic. So it makes sense that the internet is in a bit of a spin about GTA 6's more mature and restrained take on its eponymous crime. A quick, no-frills getaway in a vehicle you've hijacked on the road isn't always the most effective option. A mindless crime spree on the streets of Leonida is not a simple thing to pull off, nor an easy thing to live down. In this game, actions have consequences, and an ill-timed or ill-judged car jacking can quickly and efficiently put an end to your criminal ambitions. That's not to say you cannot simply steal cars. Of course you can: the option to saunter up to an occupied vehicle and jack it from its registered owner is available to you from the very beginning of the game. But the citizens of Leonida aren't going to take your wanton act of foolishness lying down; many of the motorists in the county will fight back, pull a piece on you, or run you over mid-robbery attempt. Even if you are lucky to find one of the more pliant residents of the city, you might find something peculiar is happening in their car. I jacked a woman in the city over the weekend, and the cat she was ferrying from place to place decided to attack me, causing me to crash. I've heard other people say they've had muffled cries coming from the boot of the car where someone is transporting a hostage, or incidents where they've jacked the same person multiple times, leading to the poor car's owner to have a breakdown in the middle of the city. That cat event, the team here at Eurogamer has worked out, is an early game trigger - it seems stealing random cars early in the game will increase the chance of this encounter occurring. Rockstar's guiding hand is more visible here, then, in trying to teach you a lesson: don't steal cars. You're given your own - Jason's two-door coupé utility, a Vapid Creado - that I actually formed quite an emotional bond with in the opening 10-or-so hours of the game. 'Look after this car,' Rockstar insists, tutorialising you how to repair it, customise it, make it all pretty so it's in good condition when you go pick up Lucia for the first time. Shortly after the 10 hour marker, narrative events whisk you away elsewhere and you're given a 'slim jim', a long, thin tool that allows you to break into locked cars - something you could only do with a quick elbow jab before. The benefit here is two-fold; you can break into cars without setting off their alarms, and without breaking glass and lowering their resale value (something quite important in the earlier sections of the game). So, it takes you until Chapter 2 to start being able to more reliably and consistently break into vehicles. Good. And it'll take even longer to break into keyless vehicles. We're in 2026 after all, and it's heavily implied this is when GTA 6 is also set - it stands to reason that many cars run keyless fobs, and your old-school tools won't cut it if you want to break into a Zorruso, rather than an old Vapid truck. But then, even when you're well-armed and ready to start an illustrious new career as Vice City's most nefarious car thief, there's more to consider. Most modern cars also come with trackers: standard trackers simply prevent you modding cars you don't own (not an issue you'll face very often), but advanced trackers are more problematic. Boosting a car with an advanced tracker immediately alerts the cops to your location, and they close in on you fast . The only answer to this problem is flooring it, and outspeeding the signal ping the tracker is sending out: you need to drive fast and cleanly in order to stay mobile long enough for the tracker to deactivate, and this often incurs damage that makes selling these cars to fences a less viable option. You can't even sell cars with trackers installed at all to some fences until you're much, much further into the game. So, long story short, stealing cars is a faff in GTA 6. But I like that. I like that Rockstar has evolved the gameplay formula to more accurately reflect the state of the world in 2026. Modern problems require modern answers, and given that Rockstar has gone above and beyond in its creation of a sandbox simulation of Florida , I feel the immersion would be broken by just being able to saunter up to any car you want and break into it. No, needing a 'slim jim' or a key cloner - or needing to case my victims properly before trying to jack them - makes for a better game as far as I'm concerned. It makes me roleplay Jason and Lucia better, it makes me engage with the game's systems more, it makes me appreciate the cars that I do have whilst I have them. It also improves the flow of the game and how I interact with missions. I recently played GTA: Vice City , and after most missions were wrapped up, I would simply fling the nearest motorist onto the sidewalk, hop in their car, and drive away into the Malibu-styled sunset. I can't simply do that in GTA 6: I need to think about my getaway options, whether there's heat on my car, and where my next best (and cheapest) ride is going to be if a robbery or raid goes awry. sources.title: GTA 6 laptop password and where to find Auntie's Place in La Perle
sources.text: Solve Vanessa's laptop puzzle in the Vice City apartment. If you've looked around the apartment you inherited from Vanessa in GTA 6 's third chapter, you might've noticed her abandoned laptop in the bedroom requires a password. You can't manually enter it, you have to choose from a series of guesses. Rather than just endlessly inputting random options, you can find the password by investigating two objects located in the apartment: Now head back to the laptop, interact with it, and choose these three words in succession: This is because Muffins is her dog, she's a queen (illustrated by the drawing), and 15 because… well, I guess she needed a number and chose her class reunion. If you tab across in the laptop, you can read Vanessa's messages, which give a clue as to what happened to her. You'll also find a mysterious message that mentions "Auntie's Place in La Perle" and gives you a code to use. The garage this code unlocks is just around the corner from Aunt Zola's Soul Food in the La Perle district of Vice City. Keep going down the street, turn right onto the main road where the Twa Ponya tattoo shop is on the left side. Drive a little way down, but before you reach Aline's Thrift Store, turn right into a little parking area with a take-out restaurant labelled as Auntie's Place, with a little awning. The garage is over on its right. Enter the safe code just below the graffiti bow on the right side and you'll unlock the Del Rio Boulevard Garage and Vanessa's Pink Growler. You can either keep the Growler, or sell it to Moses for $14,750 if you want to free up the spot for another car. sources.title: Where to find Auntie's Place in La Perle in GTA 6
sources.text: Auntie's Place is a restaurant in Grand Theft Auto 6 , but it's also a clue to another location from the laptop in the Vice City apartment. Unfortunately, Auntie's Place is extremely difficult to find, as it's not marked on the map. All we know about Auntie's Place is that it's in La Perle, and La Perle is a fairly large region. However, you'll need to find it, as there's a hidden reward just beside it that is well worth your while. Here's the exact location of Auntie's Place in GTA 6 's La Perle region, so you can use the code and get yourself a sweet new ride and a free garage. Auntie's Place is a restaurant just off Del Rio Blvd in south La Perle . It's also southeast of Aline's Thrift Store and east of TWA Ponya Tattoo . There's actually a similarly named restaurant just southwest of this location named Aunt Zola's Soul Food, so make sure you're at the right location. After you make it to Auntie's Place, walk a bit further down the road and you'll see a white garage. To the right of the garage door, you'll find a keypad with a small pink ribbon graffiti above it. Enter the 92665 code in the keypad to open the garage door and voilà! You've got your hands on your very own Vanessa's Growler, a baby pink Pfister Growler. This is a standout vehicle, so it's one more added to the collection. What's even better is that this becomes another garage you can use to store vehicles in, without having to spend any money/ If you're just getting started in GTA 6 , we have plenty of guides to help you live the high life in Leonida. sources.title: Where to find the UFO dream house in GTA 6
sources.text: If you're looking for the UFO dream house location in Grand Theft Auto 6 , that means you've already seen the UFO itself once. This unmarked optional mission begins when you investigate an abandoned car at the side of the road, follow a trail of clothes strewn on the floor, then discover a woman in a rather unfortunate situation, being beamed up into the sky. The next time you go to sleep, a concerning dream sequence happens, with one part of it showing somewhere in Leonida depicted onto what is supposed to be planet Earth. To continue the UFO storyline, you must find this unassuming building, located near a bridge and a rudimentary airstrip. If you want to know exactly where it is, you're in luck: I've found the UFO dream house location in GTA 6 , so keep reading to learn where it is. Even though the first UFO encounter happens in Port Gellhorn, the UFO dream house location is down south near Key Lento, where GTA 6 began. Specifically, it's directly north of Gambit Bay and south of Hamlet , a stone's throw northeast of the airstrip that is running north-to-south and is visible on the map. If you approach by road, you'll see a brown sign for the Grassrivers Pelican Valley recreation area. Take a left and go through to Southpoint airfield , ignoring the signs for the restricted area. The gate is locked, but you can get through by running around to the left and jumping over part of the chainlink fence that doesn't have any barbed wire at the top. Go around to the other side of the building to find the front entrance. From here, you're back reliving the dream you encountered, except everything is somewhat decrepit. This has one of the most entertaining endings to any encounter I've found so far in GTA 6 , so sit back and enjoy! sources.title: GTA 6 Tyrone Mission Walkthrough: Where to Find Tyrone
sources.text: This mission introduces you to the Kitty Litter subplot in GTA 6 Tyrone is a short mission in GTA 6 that introduces you to a prominent side character. After you finish Tyrone, you’ll have a new mission chain to complete, but more importantly, you’ll have someone to sell your stash to. Here’s everything you need to know about finding Tyrone and completing the mission. Need even more GTA 6 guides? Then check out our GTA 6 Guide Hub . Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. To start the Tyrone mission, you need to play as Jason Duval during Chapter 3. Once the mission becomes available, look for the pink TR marker on your map. This will lead you to Tyrone’s apartment complex in La Perle, Vice City. Head upstairs to the second-floor walkway and approach Tyrone’s apartment door. Knock when the interaction prompt appears. You’ll initially be questioned by one of Tyrone’s people inside, but simply give your name and ask for Tyrone. You’ll then be allowed inside to speak with Tyrone. During the conversation, Tyrone explains that a new synthetic drug called Kitty Litter is spreading throughout Vice City and taking customers away from his business. You may remember it as the drug you and Lucia took during Day Release as you raced through the streets of Vice City. He wants Jason to help discover who’s cooking the substance so that he can get in on the action. Tyrone’s hairdresser identifies a man named Charles as a potential lead. After the conversation, Dook sends Jason a text message containing Charles’s address and photograph. This completes the Tyrone meeting and pushes you directly into the next mission, Here, Kitty Kitty. There isn’t a cash reward or trophy for completing the meeting. However, it unlocks the next part of Tyrone’s storyline.

sources.title: Where to find the Silent Hill hotel in GTA 6
sources.text: In my restless playthrough, I see that town. In my restless playthrough, I see that town. The Silent Hill hotel is one of the secrets you can stumble upon in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Like the meeting with Dave and Beelzebub , you can miss the chance to enter this specific hotel and experience the creepy event that takes place inside. From the outside, it looks like a regular building, but after you visit this place, Leonida will literally change for a while. Besides, there's a safe waiting for you to open and a unique reward to collect. If you're interested in checking out this mysterious place, here's where to find the Silent Hill hotel in GTA 6 . Below, we also explain the Marbelle Hotel safe code location . You start the Silent Hill event in GTA 6 by visiting the Marbelle Hotel in Crosstown, Vice City . The area is on the northern side of the city , southwest of Bayside. The Marbelle Hotel is an old building beside Pizza Pete . To enter the hotel, you must use the door on the east side . In the initial room, you will come across a safe behind a desk, but nothing else of importance. Keep climbing the stairs until you reach the top floor , where the event will start. Note that if you visit the hotel as a couple, only the character you're controlling will enter the hotel. After you leave it, you will receive a message from your partner asking where you have been. Also, visiting the hotel a second doesn't seem to trigger the event again. If you go too far from the hotel after the event starts, the fog will disperse, and the city will return to normal. Even if you're not into supernatural experiences, you should visit the Marbelle Hotel. Inside, there's a safe containing $234 and the Crowex Ambassador 'Breakfast' luxury watch . To open it, you need a six-digit code , which you can find in two ways. The first one is on the staircase where the event starts and red signs appear on the wall . If you look at the wall to your left while climbing the stairs, you will see the drawing of a hand with an eye in its palm. Above it, you will find six numbers. If you got scared by the weird signs on the walls and were not paying attention to what was written on them, don't worry. You have another chance to find the code by heading to the roof and looking for the notes left on the ground on the northwestern side. Read them and you will find the same six digits. At both locations, you will find the same code: 955214 . Return to the safe, enter the code to open it and collect the rewards. sources.title: Judge Lets Hacker Behind Massive GTA 6 Leak of 2022 Go Free With a Warning: 'Don't Let This Happen Again'
sources.text: The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak in September 2022 has been released on license with a strong warning from the judge. Having already served the majority of his seven year sentence, Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford in the United Kingdom, was allowed to go free, conditionally. According to the BBC , the judge warned Kurtaj: "Don't let this happen again." Kurtaj attempted to extort GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games in 2022. After socially engineering his way into the company Slack, the now 21-year-old threatened to release clips of the unfinished game unless Rockstar paid a ransom. He pleaded guilty to the hacking offenses , which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, earlier this week. ⚖️ Arion Kurtaj, 21, has been convicted today for targeting major international companies, hacking into their private systems, stealing information and data, and causing millions of dollars in losses. 📰 https://t.co/UvJTCFWnct https://t.co/3CoLIw7dDs Originally, Kurtaj was sentenced to an indefinite stay in a prison hospital due to his autism diagnosis. After reconsideration, he was deemed fit to stand trial and spent the remainder of his time in a traditional prison, starting in January. With his release, Kurtaj has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order, which restricts his interactions online, barring him from using social apps like Telegram and Discord, in an attempt to prevent him working with hacker groups. The order will last for five years. The hack happened while Kurtaj was already under police protection in a Travelodge with his computer confiscated. During his stay, he used an Amazon Fire Stick and the hotel television to hack Rockstar, Revolut, and Uber. The GTA 6 hack saw him steal 90 clips of an unfinished build well before Rockstar was ready to show gameplay from its anticipated open-world sequel, which launched last week. It resulted in the first major GTA 6 leak, as early gameplay footage was shared online. Here, we saw dual protagonists Jason and Lucia for the first time. These clips were shared under the online name TeaPotUberHacker. It would be over a year before Rockstar finally showed the protagonists itself, and even longer until we got an official gameplay reveal, which was only shared in August of this year. "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code," he said in the company Slack. When the company didn’t respond, he released the files, costing the company $5 million in damages. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? sources.title: Hacker behind GTA 6 leak released as judge says "don't let this happen again"
sources.text: Arion Kurtaj, the now 21-year-old hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak of 2022, has been released from prison, as a judge warns that he shouldn't try this kind of hack again. Kurtaj was 16 years old when his hacks against Rockstar began alongside other members of hacking group Lapsus$. Following the release of at least 90 videos featuring early GTA 6 gameplay , Kurtaj was deemed psychiatrically unfit for trial and was eventually sentenced to a lifetime stay in a secure hospital because of his severe autism. Rockstar said that the hack had cost it $5 million . But Kurtaj's status changed in January, when he was transferred to a standard prison ahead of a planned retrial . Last week, he pleaded guilty to hacks against Rockstar and others . Kurtaj has been given a seven-year sentence and released on the same day, as the BBC reports. He had already served the majority of that sentence during his time in the secure hospital and prison. The judge, Mr. Justice Turner, told Kurtaj "you are a very talented young man," but offered a warning: "Don't let this happen again." The hacker has been released on license which, for my fellow Americans, is essentially a form of parole. He's been given a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting him from using online services including Telegram and Discord. Of course, this isn't the only hacking incident Rockstar is dealing with. Ahead of launch, a hacking group or individual known as Cyberleek released numerous gameplay videos from a seemingly near-final build of GTA 6. Now, Cyberleek has released an Xbox build of the game which modders are working to turn into a full-blown PC port . At this point, it's possible that an unofficial GTA 6 PC port could land before Rockstar can deliver an official version. GTA 6 update gives players losing progress to crashes a lifeline – and it looks like the first-person and 60fps glitches are safe for now Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator. sources.title: GTA 6 Hacker Officially Walks Free After Judge's Final Warning
sources.text: His Rockstar hacking spree is over, and the judge has made it clear that there won’t be a sequel The man responsible for one of the biggest Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks is finally out of prison, and the judge had one very simple message for him: Don't do it again, mister. Arion Kurtaj, now 21, was released under supervision after being sentenced to seven years in prison for a series of cybercrimes committed as a teenager, according to the BBC . The hacker, a member of the notorious Lapsus$ gang, pleaded guilty to breaking into several major companies, including Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut. Kurtaj pulled off the Rockstar breach in 2022 while staying at a Travelodge in Bicester, England — and while under police protection and on bail for other hacking offenses. With his computer confiscated, he reportedly used an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel's television, along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, to access Rockstar's internal systems. He stole company data, including 90 clips showing nearly an hour of gameplay from the unfinished GTA 6 . He then broke into Rockstar's Slack messaging system and threatened to release the game's source code unless the company contacted him on Telegram. When Rockstar refused, Kurtaj published the stolen material online under the username TeaPotUberHacker. The breach reportedly cost Rockstar $5 million to recover from, plus thousands of hours of staff time. It also revealed that Lucia would be one of the game's playable protagonists, a detail Rockstar had been keeping under wraps. Kurtaj's path from hospital custody to release was unusual: His release comes with a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting his online activity, including banning him from Telegram and Discord. Kurtaj's defense team argued that his autism spectrum disorder played a role in his offending, explaining that he found the online world more comfortable than face-to-face interactions. Judge Mr Justice Turner acknowledged Kurtaj's abilities during sentencing, telling him, "You are a very talented young man." He then delivered the warning that perhaps sums up the hearing best: "Don't let this happen again." Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. As of launch day, the game has sold 32.5 million copies and generated $3.79 billion in revenue, according to publisher Take-Two Interactive.

sources.title: God of War Laufey's Faye actor jumps from games to live-action, as Amazon casts Deborah Ann Woll in upcoming series
sources.text: After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series. Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first showed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey. Amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir. Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course. There's no release date yet for the show, but it's said to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back. Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis. "We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon." While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back , too. "Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad."

stories.title: This '90s-inspired horror game has one of the coolest post-apocalyptic worlds I've ever seen
stories.summary: Plus you can experience it all from the comfort of your campervan.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: This '90s-inspired horror game has one of the coolest post-apocalyptic worlds I've ever seen
sources.text: Plus you can experience it all from the comfort of your campervan. I often find myself thinking where the best place to survive a zombie apocalypse would be. A walled-off stone house would certainly make for some good defenses, a boat would be great—but only if the zombies didn't pull a Fear the Walking Dead—or you could spend the end of the world in a camper van. That would certainly be whimsical. You do just this in The Road of Dust and Sorrow's demo , although it's certainly not as whimsical as I first imagined it to be. You see, in this 2D horror game you have bigger responsibilities than just keeping yourself alive, you also have a young daughter to look out for as well. This isn't an easy task. Supplies are dwindling, zombie-like humans infected by addictive chemicals amble across the land in search of more dust, but they'll settle for your blood instead. Plus there's this creepy Pastor who's definitely up to something very bad. I only got one glimpse of him in the demo and he was surrounded by a lot of gore and eldritch horror, so I've just decided that staying away from him is probably for the best. But you can't hunker down and forget about all these terrors, because you have a daughter to feed and protect. So I spent most of my time in the demo gathering food, medical supplies, and trying to locate an item that may just grant us safe passage to the only sanctuary humanity has left. The dev, Painted Black Games, says it took inspiration from horror series like Silent Hill and Resident Evil for The Road of Dust and Sorrow, and while I haven't come across anything particularly traumatic in a Silent Hill sense yet (although I wouldn't be surprised to see that here) I can see the through line to Resident Evil. The action is smooth, accurate, and rewarding—which surprised me as I usually don't vibe with 2D gunplay, sometimes the controls are too finicky, but it certainly works here. Head-shotting the zombies is incredibly satisfying, as is kicking them to the floor and beating them with a baseball bat. Then there are the puzzles. I didn't come across too many, but the ones I did find were very rewarding. It's not rocket science, but the solutions aren't always obvious either. They are, however, very intuitive; you can do a lot with a little, something I very much appreciate. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. But my favourite aspect of The Road of Dust and Sorrow has to be just how cool this post-apocalyptic world is. Maybe it's the pixel art, but it manages to look dilapidated and creepy while also being oddly pretty to look at. I was searching an abandoned warehouse full of zombies and rotting cargo while thinking to myself that with a bit of elbow grease this place could really scrub up. If you want pretty and cosy, though, the campervan is where it's at. I didn't spend as much time as I would have liked to there, but it managed to feel like a real home—the only safe place left in this world. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Elie is a news writer with an unhealthy love of horror games—even though their greatest fear is being chased. When they're not screaming or hiding, there's a good chance you'll find them testing their metal in metroidvanias or just admiring their Pokemon TCG collection. Elie has previously worked at TechRadar Gaming as a staff writer and studied at JOMEC in International Journalism and Documentaries – spending their free time filming short docs about Smash Bros. or any indie game that crossed their path. sources.title: ‘It was the coolest thing I’d ever seen’: The story of Rez, 25 years on
sources.text: On its 25th anniversary, the developers behind Segaâs cult classic tell its story – and reveal why its sequel was cancelled Itâs August 2024. I’m riding through the neon-soaked streets of Tokyoâs Shibuya Ward in a Porsche, with the director of one of my favorite games at the wheel. We’re heading to his home, where he’s promised to show me beta builds that have never been seen before, and details on its canned sequel. There’s no shortage of hard work involved in covering video games, but every so often you have one of those days that makes you stop and think: wow, I’m lucky to do this. This was one of them. For me, Rez was a revelatory experience that arrived during a formative moment in my life. I was about to turn 16, leave school, and enter a hedonistic life of clubbing, music, and the human connection that comes with it. At the same time, my gaming habits had broadened into a more eclectic mix of multiplatform games, with publications like Edge encouraging me to think more about them as an artistic medium. It was inevitable, then, that I’d eventually take a chance on an electric arthouse shooter from the arcade masters at Sega . I went in blind, and discovering its abstract wireframes and interactive techno beats for myself was a deeply affecting experience. It was like simultaneously conducting a Chemical Brothers album and the Ministry of Sound light show, behind the controls of a Space Harrier machine, in a combo only video games could power. To view Rez as simply a shooter is to completely miss its meaning. On the surface, it shares much with on-rails arcade games like Panzer Dragoon and Star Fox , tasking players with blasting their way through waves of enemies on route to a spectacular boss. But these familiar mechanics are a vehicle for something more transcendent. UGAâs young team were trying to do something few commercially developed games had attempted before. Rezâs central concept is synaesthesia, the phenomenon of one sensory experience triggering another, like sounds provoking certain shapes and colors. The player is treated as a participant in a performance, with the gameâs licensed music responding to every dispatched enemy with a hi-hat or synthesizer, like you’re some sort of Tron-age conductor. All the while, its pulsing, Kandinsky-inspired visuals move in harmony with the audio, and your game controller passes the vibrations through your body, as if youâve plugged the Dreamcast into your own auxiliary port. There was simply nothing else like Rez at the time. It isn’t hyperbole to say that United Game Artists’ extraordinary sensory alchemy fundamentally changed how I, and many others of a similar age, viewed video games and what they could be. Its sales werenât spectacular, but Rezâs cultural impact makes it as valuable as any blockbuster. “It isn’t hyperbole to say that United Game Artists’ extraordinary sensory alchemy fundamentally changed how I, and many others of a similar age, viewed video games and what they could be.” Rez mattered because it showed, at a time when creators were obsessed with emulating Hollywood, that video games could create experiences that other entertainment mediums couldnât replicate. With its Y2K-inspired aesthetic, arcade-coded design, and deep reverence for late 90s club culture, Rez is staunchly a creation of its time, but itâs also absolutely timeless. To this day, Iâll regularly throw some headphones on, or a VR headset, and blast through Area 3, with its thumping Ken Ishii techno, or if Iâm in a more energetic mood, the evolutionary rollercoaster of Adam Freelandâs finale, and go beyond synaesthesia. âI do think as time has marched on, the game has become more celebrated and dear to people than when it was originally released,â producer Tetsuya Mizuguchi tells me in a meeting room at his latest studio, Enhance (he wasnât the one driving the car, by the way â weâll get to that later). âWhen we were making it too, towards the end of development, it felt more like the start of something than the end of a project for me personally, but I didn’t really know what it was the start of. I think in many ways, because it was this primitive experience, because it didn’t fit exactly into one genre convention, perhaps one of the reasons it took some time for the adulation to come to the fore has a lot to do with it took people some time to find the words that allowed them to accurately describe what they liked about the experience.â It wasnât just the players who struggled to verbalize what that Rez experience meant, Mizuguchi says. âLooking back at myself and the development team, we had trouble when we were making it, trying to express what the team was and what we were after. âBack then, we’d spend a lot of time doing things like going to electronic music clubs and observing the crowds there, and the kind of different types of reactions they’d have as music would change, and what would move them, and trying to kind of pick up clues from that sort of reaction and human experience that we were trying to then apply into Rez. âBecause we were young, because we were fairly inexperienced, we were really operating a lot more off of intuition about what this game was going to become and how we were going to get there and what we were borrowing from these sort of observed human experiences. And so, in that sense, not just for the players, but for ourselves, it’s kind of taken these 25 years to better define what we were trying to go after and what made it special.â Mizuguchi describes the circumstances surrounding Rez’s development as something of a ‘perfect storm’, much of which was deliberately engineered. The genesis of Rez, or ‘K-Projekt’ as it was first known, required a moment of inspiration and an unconventional work environment. The embers of the idea came from a spontaneous road trip. In the mid-90s, Mizuguchi was traveling back from a visit to Mercedes in Germany, where he’d been researchin

sources.title: How to steal the Declasse Vamos in GTA 6
sources.text: Grab the code to unlock the garage and steal the car for Moses. The Declasse Vamos is one of the many cars Moses asks you to steal for him in GTA 6 , but like the BF Bandito , it's a little trickier than just grabbing it. When you reach the map marker, you'll realise the car is locked in a garage that requires a specific code to open it. The code to the door is 2727 and this is fixed. The way you discover this is by sneaking inside the trailer and looking at the number plate on the wall to the left of the window, just above the guy snoozing in the chair. Enter the code to open the garage, break in with the slimjim, then hit the button to open the door. I personally incapacitated all of the people behind the trailer, so chances are they will pursue you or start shooting if you don't, once you try to drive out of there. Now take the car back to Moses, being careful on the way, to earn $4,100ish for top condition. sources.title: Why can't you play darts in GTA 6 when you could in previous games? Because Rockstar "didn't have the resources" to do it to a standard it'd be happy with
sources.text: If you've been a fan of Grand Theft Auto for a while, you might have noticed a strange absence in GTA 6. While the game is packed full of different activities, the recurring pastime of darts is missing, having been present in GTA 5 , GTA Online , and GTA 4. The reason for the lack of darts in Grand Theft Auto 6? Well, according to Rockstar North co-studio lead Rob Nelson, it's a simple case of Rockstar having too little time and resources to make it to a high standard. Nelson told VGC : "The darts one is a contentious one. Even we... You hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to." Nelson elaborated that since Red Dead Redemption 2 , Rockstar has taken to expanding what were small mini-games into full-on activities. He pointed to basketball in GTA 6 as an example, which you can play in a way that feels like an extension of gameplay with "fluid" movement. Even if it's a relatively small chunk of the game, a lot of time went into making it feel like "a game in its own right", Nelson said. And the same is true of pool . "A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right. Darts is one we just didn't get to," Nelson said. The studio "didn't have the resources" to include it in the game and have it up to par. "It's better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough," he said. Even without darts, there are plenty of side activities in Grand Theft Auto 6 that help expand Vice City. This includes diving and treasure hunting and fishing , both of which you unlock near the start of the game. If you're looking for a guide of all there is to do in the game, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough is a good place to start. We've also got a breakdown of all the GTA 6 cheats if you needed an extra hand getting through the game.
